scope: Independent audit, read-only against the Target. Covered every 10.1 finding (V-1 to V-10), every workflow 7.1 to 7.10 (key steps traced in source), and all 14 section 14 questions. Sections 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 9, 10.2, 11, 15 and 16 were sampled, prioritising auth and authorization statements, defaults and settings, counts and enumerations: all 31 scheduled jobs in 16.7 were compared with services/cron/tasks_actions.go, tasks_basic.go and tasks_extended.go, and the entry-point totals were reconciled with facts.json. Not audited: section 12 diagrams, section 13 glossary, most UI-n rows (only UI-3, UI-26, UI-27 and the count of 27), 4.1 file counts (generated, covered by the Check), the 16.6 key table beyond sampling, templates and web_src. 8.4 field tables were spot-checked for User, Repository, access token, two-factor, secret and auth source. The Facts contain no smell Facts for this target.

claim: Start-up initialises git, locales, settings, storage, mailer, cache, database, models, indexers, webhooks, SSH and finally cron.
NormalRoutes mounts web routes at /, the REST API at /api/v1, the internal API at /api/internal and, when enabled, packages and Actions.
The web layer builds an auth group per request (OAuth2, deploy token and Basic only where a route opts in, optional reverse proxy, session, SSPI on Windows); a failed verification returns 401.
The API auth group is OAuth2 token, HTTP signature and Basic (plus reverse proxy when enabled); token scopes are checked by category and HTTP method.
Basic authentication tries the password field as OAuth2 token, personal access token and Actions task token first, and only then the user password when enabled.
The internal API compares the X-Gitea-Internal-Auth bearer value with the configured internal token in constant time.
Runners authenticate with a UUID and a token verified against a salted hash.

verifyAuthWithOptionsWeb blocks inactive and prohibited accounts, forces a password change, redirects anonymous users when sign-in is required, applies cross-origin protection and enforces admin-only routes.
Two-factor TOTP and WebAuthn are enforced at web sign-in.
